full_judgment: 12. The withdrawal of Taka 29 lac and odd from 4-8-82 to 31-12-82 was made by 12 cheques, Nos. 610-613,615.616,618,620, 622.626 signed by the respondent alone. Excepting two, all these cheques were mentioned by the respondent in his letters to the petitioner in Annexures J, J5, H6, K., K2, L, L5, L6, In these letters the respondent stated that cheques for certain amount, such as Tk. 3 lacs in the letter Annexure 'J' or Taka 8 lacs in the letter Annexure 'H6' were "prepared and kept ready" for the petitioner's signature, and requested him to come and subscribe his signatures thereon. Neither date nor number of any cheques was mentioned in those letters. By the cheques Nos.610, 611 and 613 an amount of Taka 7.15 lacs was withdrawn from 9-8-82 to 10-9-82, that is, after the filing, of the petition for contempt and before the Notice for contempt was issued and the amount of Tk. 22 lacs and odd was withdrawn by the other 9 cheques after the Notice was issued. All these cheques including cheques No. 611S for Taka 8 lacs are cash cheques; but the respondent in his affidavit dated 27-1-83 claimed that all cheques "were genuine, account-payee cheques." Later on he corrected this statement. The petitioner attended the firm's office on 6-8-82, 30-8-82, 6-11-82 and 26-12-82 but did not sign the cheques alleging that no certificated bills in support of the respective cheques were produced before him. He complained in his letter Annexure J(2) dated 6.8.82 that the respondent showed him some bills which were not certified by anybody and wanted him to put his signature on those bills by way of acknowledgment, but the refused. This allegation was denied by the respondent by his letter Annexure J(3). On the subsequent occasions also the same thing was repeated petitioner saying that no certificated bills were produced, and the respondent maintaining that certificated bills were produced. The petitioner there after by two letters-Annexures K and L-3 requested the respondent to forward to him the certificated bills and the corresponding cheques. But the respondent by a letter, Annexures 'K2' expressed his inability to forward the cheques and the bills on the ground of 'safety and security of the cheques and bills'. Thereupon the petitioner addressed two more letters requesting the respondent to forward Photostat copies of the certificated bills. This request was also rejected on the same ground of 'safety and security of the bills'. In view of these allegations and counter-allegations, both supported by affidavits, it was for the respondent to forward copies of the bills by registered post or through responsible officers of the firm. If the original bills were not sent on the ground of safety and security there was no question of 'safety and security in the case, of copies of the bills. Respondent's refusal to forward copies of the bills raises a presumption that either there was no certificated bill in support of the cheques, or if there were any bills they contained something which would not stand scrutiny and verification if sent to the petitioner. The very purpose of clause (5) of our order was to keep the petitioner informed about the receipts and disbursement of money in connection with the firm's business in view of the allegations of misappropriation breach of trust and diversion of fund for the private purposes, against the Managing Partner. In view of the mandatory provision as to certificated bills as a condition for the petitioner's signature for withdrawal, the withdrawal by the respondent by these 12 cheques was not made on the basis of certificated bills in terms of clause (5).
